name: sidebar-toggle-beside-traffic-lights
description: A row that had already shed sbtoggle (a narrow sidebar) must not keep it hidden once the floating address bar takes the nav group - setNavGroupInRow's inRow=false branch now clears navgone itself, since layoutNavRow (the only other code that clears it) early-returns for as long as the group is away. navgone is forced here rather than reached by narrowing the sidebar - the width ladder that produces it is already covered by sidebar-nav-row-test.mjs; this scenario proves the real browser renders the restored toggle inside the caption hole and that a click on it still reaches the window rather than starting a drag.

actions.note: let the space and its tab render before the first eval targets /sidebar
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot

actions.expression: (() => { const row = document.querySelector('.sbnav'); if (!row) { return 'no row'; } return [...row.children].map((b) => b.className).join('|'); })()
actions.note: Baseline: the floating bar is down, so the row should carry its ordinary five controls untouched by this fix.
the top-left corner with the floating bar down - the toggle sits beside back/forward/reload here

actions.expression: (() => { const t = document.querySelector('.sbnav .sbtoggle'); if (!t) { return 'no-toggle'; } t.classList.add('navgone'); return t.className; })()
actions.note: Simulates the reported precondition: a sidebar narrow enough to have shed the toggle before the handover (visibleNavButtons sheds it below TWO_AND_MENU, reachable at kMinSidebarWidth per sidebar-nav-row-test.mjs). The width ladder itself is unit-tested; this scenario is only about what the real handover does once navgone is already set.
opens the floating address bar (devbar), which drives atriumSetDevBarShown(true) -> setNavGroupInRow(row, false)
THE GATE for the handover itself: back/forward/reload leave the sidebar row for the devbar.

actions.expression: (() => { const t = document.querySelector('.sbnav .sbtoggle'); if (!t) { return 'no-toggle'; } return t.classList.contains('navgone') ? 'still-navgone' : 'visible'; })()
actions.note: THE FIX: before this change the toggle stayed navgone forever here, because layoutNavRow - the only other code that clears it - early-returns while inRow is false.
the top-left corner with the floating bar up - the toggle must sit beside the traffic lights, alone, inside the carved caption hole (x 82..196)

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.sbnav .sbtoggle'); if (!b) { return 'no-button'; } b.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerover', {bubbles: true, pointerType: 'mouse'})); return 'hovered'; })()
actions.note: The second clause: starts the hover-hint delay (HOVER_DELAY_MS=600ms, hint-triggers.js). NATIVE_HINT_ROUTES maps /sidebar to the HintOverlayWidget path unconditionally, so the bubble itself renders on the /hint route, never as a DOM node here - hint.js's showHint native branch.
Gate only, no content check yet - covers the 600ms delay, the chrome.send round trip, and (first hover of the run) HintOverlayWidget constructing its own WebContents.

actions.expression: (() => { const el = document.querySelector('.hint'); if (!el) { return 'no-hint'; } const text = el.querySelector('.hint-text')?.textContent || ''; const keys = [...el.querySelectorAll('.hint-keys .ov-key')].map((k) => k.textContent).join(''); return text + '|' + keys; })()
actions.note: Read the rendered chord, do not assume it: compare against atrium_native_hotkey_defaults.cc's kToggleSidebar row ("cmd+s", glyphed by CommandBarShortcutGlyphs) - the true source of NativeHotkeyMap's default, since this scenario loads no hotkeys.json override.
the hint bubble HintOverlayWidget draws while hovering the restored toggle with the floating bar still up - read this frame directly rather than trusting eval_equals alone.

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.sbnav .sbtoggle'); if (!b) { return 'no-button'; } b.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerout', {bubbles: true, pointerType: 'mouse', relatedTarget: document.body})); return 'unhovered'; })()
actions.note: Clears the hint before the click below, so its own hide/show round trip does not land in the middle of the toggle click.

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.sbnav .sbtoggle'); if (!b) { return 'no-button'; } b.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', {bubbles: true})); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: LAST: proves the moved toggle is still hit-testable rather than starting a window drag - a click outside the carved caption hole never reaches the DOM at all, so any answer other than 'no-button' already means the click landed. The vlog assertion below confirms the click reached ToggleSidebar.

assertions.expected: "sbtd|nb sbtoggle|nb first sbback navdim|nb sbfwd navdim|nb sbreload"
assertions.note: Unchanged from the lab's own order while the floating bar is down. navdim on back/forward here is a fresh tab with no history to go back or forward to - orthogonal to this fix.
The toggle is visible next to the traffic lights once the floating bar takes the group, even though it was shed before the handover.

The second clause. ⌘S is CommandBarShortcutGlyphs("cmd+s"), the compiled-in default for kToggleSidebar (atrium_native_hotkey_defaults.cc) - this scenario stages no hotkeys.json, so NativeHotkeyMap has no override to read instead. Read the hover-hint capture directly rather than trusting this line alone: a scenario asserting its own hardcoded guess proves nothing about the live map.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: sidebar toggle requested from the chrome row
assertions.label: toggle-reached-the-window
assertions.note: The click on the restored, relocated button still reaches BrowserController::ToggleSidebar rather than starting a window drag.
